text:
Ellie: Heads up - onboarding starlark-7b (int4) shows token-level drift vs fp16 on punctuation and EOS, failing some unit prompts. Repro + short logs below, any ideas?

Omar: Can you paste the minimal repro and the diff vs fp16?

Ellie: repro:
```bash
python eval.py --model starlark-7b --quant int4 --prompt "Hello, world!" --seed 42 --batch 1
```
Outputs:
```
FP16: Hello, world!
INT4:  Hello , world !
```
Notice extra spaces around punctuation and different EOS probs.

Sasha: that smells like tokenizer/vocab index shift or rotary scaling mismatch. Did conversion set --vocab-offset or reorder embeddings? :thinking: 

Matt: Also check tokenizer.special_tokens_map and whether sentinel tokens got remapped (we saw 50256 vs 50257 issues earlier). Run `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('starlark-7b'); print(t.encode('!'))"`

Ellie: ran token id check:
```
'!': 33
'.': 13
'': 50256
```
Weird: there's an empty-string sentinel at 50256; conversion tool inserted a placeholder.

bench-bot: perf note - int4 on starlark-7b: latency 48ms/token, ppl +0.9 vs fp16 baseline on evalset v1 (brief).

Sasha: If there's a sentinel inserted at high id, KV cache index aliasing can shift rotary phase application for high token ids. Try conversion with --preserve-token-ids or run `scripts/fix_vocab_map.py --strip-placeholder`.

Omar: I'll run a quick bisect on rotary_scale (1.0 vs 1.2 vs 1.4) and headwise phase match. Ping me if you want me to run on dedicated GPU pool.

QA-Jen: Also do a logits diff script: `scripts/compare_logits.py --fp16 pathA --int4 pathB --tokens 200 --report topk` - shows whether prob mass is redistributed or just spacing.

Ellie: cool, thanks. I'll try strip-placeholder and request the bisect. I'll post results here. Filing follow-up: starlark-7b onboard ticket (T1234). @Omar @Sasha assigned. :thumbsup:
